\section{Representation change as a constrained dynamics}
\label{sec:representation}

The staple representation exposes relational coherence.  It hides the fact
that the six transports are functions of a shared link field.  The link
representation exposes exact realizability and locality.  It hides the
Fr\'echet geometry of the local residual energy.  Neither description is
wrong; each makes different operations elementary.

The pair of maps
\[
 C^1\xrightarrow{\ d_1\ }C^2
 \xrightarrow{\ (C_6O_\ell S_\ell,E_\ell)\ }
 V_\ell\oplus C^2_{\Ext}
\]
makes the information balance explicit.  Projection onto $V_\ell$ forgets
external curvature.  The minimum-spill form $h_\ell$ measures the least cost
of reconstructing a link variation after that forgetting.  In this sense,
$h_\ell$ is a quantitative defect of local representability.

Three lessons follow.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item A gauge-covariant coordinate can carry physical information without
being a gauge-invariant variable by itself.  The staples transform
covariantly; their mutual dispersion is invariant.
\item A useful effective operation need not lift as the same local operation
on microscopic variables.  The missing information reappears as spillover.
\item ``Local'' should be typed by representation.  Centering is local in a
star coordinate, whereas realizing a centered displacement is a constrained
problem on the surrounding complex.
\end{enumerate}

This is a small, finite-dimensional instance of representational dynamics: a
description is characterized not only by its variables, but also by the maps
that produce it, the information those maps discard, and the obstruction to
lifting operations back through them.  The calculation does not by itself
solve an infrared problem.  It does identify one compatibility cost that any
repair-based constructive argument must either pay or cancel through a more
coordinated operation.
